item.title: Exact rational certificates and a Lean formalization of the eleven-variable Vasc inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the cyclic sum $\sum_{i=0}^{10}(x_i-x_{i+1})/(x_{i+1}+x_{i+2})$ is nonnegative for every strictly positive real eleven-tuple, with indices taken modulo eleven. Clearing denominators reduces the problem to a homogeneous polynomial. Subtracting the smallest coordinate then separates the proof into nonnegativity of a common-translation derivative and nonnegativity on a full boundary face. We supply exact rational polynomial certificates in Gram-matrix form for both statements. The derivative certificate uses a linear multiplier, centered monomials and cyclic averaging; the boundary certificate uses a strictly positive quadratic multiplier and uncentered monomials. Their verification requires 6,069 cyclic coefficient comparisons and 34,304 literal coefficient comparisons. All 606 certificate matrices are certified by integer congruences with strictly diagonally dominant images. A Lean 4 development formally verifies the certificate checks and their connection to the original inequality. The exact certificate data, replay programs, and formal sources are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Dakai Guo, Ruichen Qiu, Yichuan Cao, Ruyong Feng, Xiao-Shan Gao

item.title: An Infinite Family of Ap\'ery-like Recurrences for Euler's Constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.13919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Euler's constant $\gamma$, also known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant, remains one of the most elusive constants in mathematics. Despite extensive study, its irrationality is still unproven, and Ap\'ery-like approximations of it are remarkably scarce. We present a novel identity that expresses $\gamma$ in terms of a Meijer G-function and its first few derivatives. This identity is then generalized and used to systematically generate infinitely many Ap\'ery-like approximations of $\gamma$ using a Conservative Matrix Field construction based on the Meijer G-function.
item.dc:creator: Rotem Kalisch, Tali Monderer, Elyasheev Leibtag, Shachar Weinbaum, Michael Shalyt, Ido Kaminer

item.title: PySymmetry: A Sage/Python Framework for the Symmetry Reduction of Linear G-Equivariant Systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.19479v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite the prevalence of symmetry in scientific linear systems, these structural properties are often underutilized by standard computational software. This paper introduces PySymmetry, an open-source Sage/Python framework that implements classical representation theory to simplify G-equivariant linear systems. PySymmetry uses projection operators to generate symmetry-adapted bases, transforming equivariant operators into a more efficient block-diagonal form. Its functionalities include defining and reducing representations, calculating multiplicities, and obtaining the explicit block structure. We demonstrate PySymmetry's versatility through three case studies: a chemistry application, a numerical benchmark on the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation that achieved a performance increase of over 17x compared to standard methods, and a symbolic investigation that enabled the first complete analytical classification of a challenging problem in celestial mechanics. Designed for seamless integration with libraries like NumPy and SciPy, PySymmetry offers a powerful, user-friendly tool for exploring symmetries in theoretical and applied contexts. ```
item.dc:creator: Leon D. da Silva, Marcelo P. Santos
